articles.title: High Court Rules Against Hopwood DePree in Ownership Dispute Over Hopwood Hall
articles.excerpt: The High Court in Manchester has ruled that Rochdale Council acted fairly in denying ownership of Hopwood Hall to Hopwood DePree, a descendant of the original owners.
articles.content_html:
A High Court ruling has determined that Rochdale Council did not act unfairly in its decision to deny ownership of Hopwood Hall to Hopwood DePree, a descendant of the family that originally built the historic property in the 1420s. The ruling concluded a two-day trial held in Manchester, where DePree had sought to overturn the council's decision to terminate an exclusivity agreement for the sale of the Grade II-listed hall.

Following the verdict, DePree expressed disappointment, stating it was a significant setback for both the community and heritage rescue groups across the UK. He indicated that his legal team is currently exploring potential next steps in response to the ruling. DePree emphasised the importance of monitoring the council's efforts to preserve and restore Hopwood Hall for public benefit.

Hopwood Hall has a rich history, having been owned by the Hopwood family until 1922, after which it changed hands multiple times. The building was used as a Catholic teacher training college until the 1980s, after which it fell into disrepair. Rochdale Council acquired the property to prevent further deterioration and has since been involved in discussions regarding its future.

The ruling may have implications for the future of Hopwood Hall, as the council continues to seek ways to restore the building and engage the community in its preservation. The next steps for both the council and DePree remain to be seen as they navigate the aftermath of this legal decision.
